name: goat_horn
revision: r2 (2026-11-10): the r1 critic's and continuity's must-fixes applied, see reviews/r1-response.md
caption: my dad vs this goat: 0 wins, 213 losses 🐐
logline: A kid whose dad gets rammed off the same cliff by the same goat every day finds out what Dad was really after the morning Dad leaves for the far mines.
question: why tf does my dad let a goat knock him off a cliff every day?
premise: A goat on the shelf above the lake has knocked Dad off the same cliff 213 times. He lands in the deep lake, climbs the stairs back up, and stands in front of it again, one step in front of a big oak, trying to dodge at the last second. He's too slow. Ida next door has a goat horn on her wall and says a goat missed her. Dad's donkey is packed for the far mines for the winter, and he said he can't go till he gets his kid one thing. The kid thinks he means a win. This morning Dad left anyway.
twist: Dad wasn't losing a grudge match. A goat drops a goat horn only when it rams a solid block, never a player, so Dad was trying to make it miss him and hit the oak: a horn for his kid, to call him from anywhere while he's away (a goat horn is heard 256 blocks off). The kid, who has watched all 213 tries and knows the tell, takes Dad's spot, steps as the goat drops its head, the goat hits the oak, out pops a GOAT HORN, he blows it, and far down the road Dad turns around.

requests.direction: [A bubbly nine-year-old kid, fast, bright and energetic, telling a friend an amazing story; not whispery, breathy or soft]
[A bubbly nine-year-old kid, fast, bright and energetic, telling a friend an amazing story; not whispery, breathy or soft]
A mountain lake. A big gruff dad, soaked to the skin, shouts a score up a cliff to his kid: full volume, cheerful, proud of it.

lines.text: A GOAT / has knocked / my DAD / off the same CLIFF / 213 TIMES.
lines.say: A goat has knocked my dad off the same cliff two hundred thirteen times.
lines.direction: one quick excited breath, already laughing at it, lean on the number

lines.text: He lands / in the LAKE. / Climbs BACK up.
lines.direction: bright and matter-of-fact, like it's the most normal thing in the world

lines.text: He tries / to DODGE. / Too SLOW.
lines.say: He tries to dodge. <short pause> Too slow.
lines.direction: fond and teasing, the last two words flat and quick, a little wince
shouted up from the water, cheerful and proud, like a high score

lines.text: IDA / has a GOAT HORN. / She says a goat / MISSED her. / Goats don't MISS.
lines.say: Ida has a goat horn. She says a goat missed her. <short pause> Goats don't miss.
lines.direction: gossipy and sure of himself, the last sentence a know-it-all shrug

lines.text: Dad's DONKEY / is packed / for the MINES. / ALL winter.
lines.say: Dad's donkey is packed for the mines. <short pause> All winter.
lines.direction: the energy dips, the last two words smaller, but still full volume

lines.text: Dad said / he can't go / till he gets me / ONE thing. / I figured / he meant a WIN.
lines.say: Dad said he can't go till he gets me one thing. <short pause> I figured he meant a win.
lines.direction: bouncing back to funny, a know-it-all shrug on the last sentence

lines.text: And this morning, / he LEFT anyway.
lines.direction: the one sad line: plain and quiet in feeling, still full volume, no whisper
a breath, then determined and proud

lines.text: I'd watched / 213 TIMES. / It dropped / its HEAD. / I STEPPED.
lines.say: I'd watched two hundred thirteen times. It dropped its head. <short pause> I stepped.
lines.direction: fast and proud of the number, then tense, each sentence a beat, the last word snapped

lines.text: BONK. / Into the OAK. / Out popped / a GOAT HORN.
lines.say: Bonk! <short pause> Into the oak. Out popped a goat horn.
lines.direction: the first word a big comic sound, then amazed, rising to the last two words

lines.text: It was / for ME. / To CALL him.
lines.say: It was for me. <short pause> To call him.
lines.direction: the penny drops: wonder on the first sentence, then sure and warm

lines.text: I BLASTED it. / Down the ROAD, / Dad turned / and WAVED.
lines.direction: bursting with joy, rising to the last word and holding it a moment
lines.say: I blasted it. Down the road, Dad turned and waved.

ending.loop: cause and effect: the 213 knocks in L01 were 213 tries at this horn
